gen-gf-offside-gf-basic: Offside never quite closes its curves, and the wide tracking lets each letter breathe. Basic sits beneath with a gentle lift from small letters to capitals, so the headline's drama has somewhere quiet to land.
gen-gf-offside-gf-changa: Commanding in its wide-tracked, level stride, Offside leads with strokes that all keep the width of a rolling-ball pen. Changa follows with sturdy, iron-tall lowercase.
gen-gf-offside-gf-epunda-sans: Expressive from the first letter, Offside cuts its open curves at one laser-sheet width and spaces them wide. And Epunda Sans answers with oversized e and a counters and trimmed sidebearings, so the daylight inside its curves is what you remember.
gen-gf-offside-gf-geom: Commanding and a bit theatrical, Offside draws every stroke like cable at one thickness, tracked wide and level. Geom's lofty lowercase band keeps the text below approachable.
gen-gf-offside-gf-inder: Expressive and wide-set, Offside even draws its g in one unchanging line. Inder keeps its cases close in height, giving that flourish a tidy, steady partner underneath.
gen-gf-offside-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Round, wired, and wide-spaced. Offside is best at bold, unclosed curves with no stroke contrast, while Kdam Thmor Pro fills the line with bowls and does its best work as sturdy, modern sans-serif text.
gen-gf-offside-gf-matemasie: Matemasie reads broad and spacious, with small entry points into its round, closed letters and little drop between capitals and lowercase. Offside, by contrast, leaves its curves open and tracks wide, and that open-versus-closed difference is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-offside-gf-mitr: Mitr reads dense and friendly, with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. Offside sets that against stroke contrast of exactly none, wide tracking and open curves, so the heading feels spacious while the text stays compact.
gen-gf-offside-gf-momo-trust-display: Open curves drawn like bent wire, set wide and level, give Offside its look. But Momo Trust Display, a sans-serif with a generous x-height and drifting letters, would carry a longer passage with a loose, easy stride.
gen-gf-offside-gf-mukta: Offside's strokes look like a bent paperclip, tracked wide and left open, with no swells in weight anywhere. It does the showy work, while Mukta's tall-bodied small letters quietly handle the reading.
